examples.en: On busy mornings I simply get by with bread.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 간편히 송금할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can send money easily with this app.
I packed light and left for the trip.
Please come dressed casually.

examples.ko: 간편히 먹을 수 있는 도시락을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a lunch box that is easy to eat.
Is there a convenient way to submit the documents?

explain: '간편하게'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '간편하게'를 쓰기도 하고, '간편히'는 안내문이나 광고 문구에서도 볼 수 있어요. 형용사는 '간편하다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '간편하게'. In speech people also say '간편하게', and '간편히' can be seen in notices and ads. The adjective is '간편하다'.

examples.en: The apartment security guard said hello.
I left the parcel with the security guard.

examples.ko: 밤에는 경비원 두 명이 건물을 지켜요.
examples.en: At night, two guards watch over the building.
The guard came to work early in the morning.

examples.ko: 저는 경비원을 불러서 문을 열어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I called the guard and asked him to open the door.
The bank's guard is kind to customers too.

explain: 아파트에서는 친근하게 '경비 아저씨'라고도 불러요. '-원'은 일하는 사람을 뜻해서 은행원, 회사원, 공무원처럼 다른 직업 이름에도 붙어요.
explain_en: In apartment buildings, people also call them 경비 아저씨 in a friendly way. The ending -원 means a worker, and it appears in job names such as 은행원, 회사원, and 공무원.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에 과속하면 아주 위험해요.
examples.en: Speeding on a rainy day is very dangerous.

examples.ko: 아버지는 운전할 때 절대 과속하지 않으세요.
examples.en: My father never speeds when he drives.
The car was speeding and got caught by the police.
Yesterday I saw a speeding car on the highway.
I almost had an accident because I was speeding.
I was worried my friend might speed.

explain: 도로의 제한 속도를 넘어 달릴 때 써요. 명사 '과속'에 다른 말을 붙여 '과속 운전', '과속 단속'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when driving over the speed limit. The noun '과속' also combines with other words, as in '과속 운전' and '과속 단속'.

examples.en: It is hard to tell the twins apart.
Can you tell real from fake?
The colors were so similar that I couldn't tell them apart.

examples.ko: 공과 사를 구별하는 사람이 좋은 직원이에요.
examples.en: A person who separates work from private matters is a good employee.
I want to distinguish the pronunciation of the two words.

examples.ko: 아이들은 아직 꿈과 현실을 구별하지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't yet tell dreams from reality.

explain: 구별하다는 둘 이상이 서로 다르다는 것을 알아보고 나누는 거예요. '구분하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 구분하다는 기준에 따라 나눈다는 느낌이 더 강하고 구별하다는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 'A와 B를 구별하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 구별하다 is to recognize that two or more things differ and tell them apart. It is close to '구분하다', which leans more toward dividing things by a standard, while 구별하다 leans toward noticing the difference. The usual pattern is 'A와 B를 구별하다'.

examples.en: I was so glad to see my friend after a long time.
In my delight, I shouted without realizing it.
He couldn't hide his delight and smiled.
I felt surprise before I felt gladness.
I was half glad and half worried.

examples.ko: 오래된 편지를 읽고 반가움과 그리움을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: Reading the old letter, I felt gladness and longing.

explain: '반갑다'에서 나온 말로, 만나거나 소식을 들었을 때의 기쁜 마음을 말해요. 그냥 '기쁨'보다 사람이나 소식과 연결된 느낌이에요. 직접 인사할 때는 명사보다 '반가워요'를 써요.
explain_en: It comes from '반갑다' and describes the happy feeling on meeting someone or hearing news. Compared with plain '기쁨', it is tied to a person or news. When greeting someone directly, say '반가워요' rather than this noun.

examples.ko: 가전제품을 사면 보증서를 꼭 받아 두세요.
examples.en: When you buy an appliance, be sure to get the warranty.
Without the warranty, it's hard to get free repairs.
The date of purchase is written on the warranty.

examples.ko: 시계가 고장 나서 보증서를 들고 서비스센터에 갔어요.
examples.en: My watch broke, so I took the warranty to the service center.
I lost the warranty. Would the receipt work?

examples.ko: 이 보증서는 일 년 동안만 효력이 있어요.
examples.en: This warranty is valid for only one year.

explain: 물건을 산 뒤 일정 기간 무료로 고쳐 준다고 약속하는 문서예요. 수리를 받는 것은 'A/S'(에이에스)라고 많이 말해요. 영수증과 함께 보관하라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a document promising free repairs for a set period after you buy something. Getting repairs is often called 'A/S' (after-sales service). People often tell you to keep it together with the receipt.

en: precaution against fire; watching out for fire

examples.en: Being careful with fire is even more important in dry weather.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 학교에서 불조심 포스터를 그려요.
examples.en: When winter comes, we draw fire-safety posters at school.

examples.ko: 불조심 기간에 소방서에서 안전 교육을 해요.
examples.en: During fire-safety week the fire station gives safety training.

examples.ko: 집을 비울 때는 불조심을 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to be careful with fire when you leave the house.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 불조심에 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you go to the mountains, you have to pay attention to fire safety.
There are signs saying 'Watch out for fire' all over the place.

explain: '불조심하세요'처럼 인사나 주의 말로도 많이 써요. 포스터나 표지판에서는 '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' 같은 표어와 함께 자주 볼 수 있어요. 더 딱딱한 말로는 '화재 예방'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is also used as a warning, as in '불조심하세요'. On posters and signs you often see it with slogans like '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' (check even a put-out fire again). A more formal expression is '화재 예방' (fire prevention).

examples.en: Please do the homework a bit faster.

examples.ko: 저는 일을 빨리해야 퇴근할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can leave work only if I get things done quickly.

examples.ko: 준비를 빨리하면 일찍 출발할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get ready quickly, we can leave early.
I did the dishes quickly and then rested.
I'm trying to make decisions quickly.
I tend to wash my face quickly in the morning.

explain: '일을 빨리하다'처럼 동작을 서두를 때 써요. '빨리 하다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 말할 때는 '빨리 가다', '빨리 먹다'처럼 부사 '빨리'를 다른 동사 앞에 붙이는 일이 더 많고, 재촉할 때는 '빨리빨리', '서둘러 주세요'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used when you hurry an action, like doing a task quickly. It can also be written with a space: '빨리 하다'. In speech, people more often put the adverb 빨리 before another verb, as in '빨리 가다' and '빨리 먹다'. To urge someone, '빨리빨리' and '서둘러 주세요' are very common.

examples.en: Please sign down here.
I signed the contract for my new place yesterday.
I pay by card and sign the receipt.
Please tell me where to sign.
Write your name and sign below.
You need an ID to sign.

explain: 일상에서는 '사인하다'도 많이 써요. 가수나 배우가 팬에게 해 주는 건 '서명'보다 '사인'이라고 해요. 도장을 찍는 건 '도장을 찍다'라고 따로 말해요.
explain_en: In daily life people also say '사인하다'. A singer or actor signing for a fan is usually '사인', not 서명. Stamping with a seal is a separate phrase, '도장을 찍다'.

en: price list; rates table; fare table

examples.en: A parking rate chart is posted at the entrance.

examples.ko: 요금표를 보고 가장 싼 것을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I looked at the price list and chose the cheapest one.
Where is the hair salon's price list posted?
The rates changed, so the price went up.

examples.ko: 요금표에 세금이 포함되어 있는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check whether tax is included in the price list.

examples.ko: 이 요금표는 한 달 전 거예요.
examples.en: This price list is from a month ago.

explain: 주차, 택시, 전화, 미용실처럼 서비스 이용료가 적힌 표를 말해요. 물건 값을 적은 표는 보통 '가격표'라고 해요. 가게나 시설 입구에 붙어 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a chart listing fees for services such as parking, taxis, phones or hair salons. A chart for goods is usually called '가격표'. It's often posted at the entrance of a shop or facility.

examples.en: Right now safety comes before everything.

examples.ko: 시간이 없으면 중요한 일부터 우선해서 하세요.
examples.en: If you are short on time, do the important things first.
More people put health first these days.
I prioritized quality over price.
I will put family before work.

examples.ko: 응급 환자를 우선하고 다른 환자는 기다려요.
examples.en: Emergency patients come first and other patients wait.

explain: 대화에서는 '우선하다'보다 '먼저 하다', '먼저 챙기다'가 더 자주 나와요. '우선하다'는 뉴스, 안내문, 회의처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '안전 우선', '고객 우선'처럼 명사 '우선'으로 줄여 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 많아요.
explain_en: In conversation people more often say 먼저 하다 or 먼저 챙기다. 우선하다 fits formal settings such as news, notices, and meetings. Even more common is the shortened noun form, as in 안전 우선 (safety first) and 고객 우선 (customer first).

en: such; of this kind; of this sort

examples.en: The situation is like this, so it can't be helped.
This is my situation, so please understand.
The results are as follows.
This kind of thing is a first for me.
The story went roughly like this.
If the plan is like this, I agree.

explain: 말할 때는 '이래요', '이런'을 더 많이 써요. '이러하다'는 발표나 글에서 '내용은 이러합니다'처럼 뒤에 나올 내용을 소개할 때 자주 보여요. '그러하다', '저러하다'와 짝이에요.
explain_en: In conversation, '이래요' and '이런' are used more. 이러하다 often appears in presentations and writing to introduce what comes next, as in '내용은 이러합니다'. It pairs with 그러하다 and 저러하다.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 새 옷을 창문 쪽에 전시해요.
examples.en: This shop displays new clothes by the window.
We displayed the pictures the students made in the hallway.
To exhibit your work, you have to apply.
I'm choosing the photos to exhibit.
Where do you want to display it?
The paintings shown at the gallery are great.

explain: 사람이나 기관이 주어일 때 써요. 물건이 주어이면 '전시되다'예요. 보러 가는 행사는 '전시회'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a person or institution is the subject. If the object is the subject, use '전시되다'. The event you visit is called '전시회'.

examples.en: The teacher designates the pages to read for homework.
The company assigned me a specific seat.
Where will you set the meeting place?
Thank you for assigning me a seat.
I pick the recipient and send the email.
It is a place the mayor designated as the new park.

explain: '정하다'보다 딱딱해서 안내문, 서류, 규칙에 자주 나와요. 여러 가운데 하나를 콕 집어 말할 때 쓰고, '지정 좌석', '지정석'처럼 명사 앞에도 붙어요.
explain_en: It sounds more formal than '정하다' and often appears in notices, documents and rules. You use it when you pick one thing out of several, and it also attaches to nouns, as in '지정 좌석' and '지정석'.

examples.en: The sea shines blue-green.
I bought a blue-green shirt.

examples.ko: 저는 청록색이 잘 어울린다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often hear that blue-green suits me.

examples.ko: 청록색 커튼으로 바꾸니까 방 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The room feels different after I changed to blue-green curtains.

examples.ko: 청록색 물감이 없어서 파랑과 초록을 섞었어요.
examples.en: I had no turquoise paint, so I mixed blue and green.

examples.ko: 이 호수는 날씨에 따라 청록색을 띠어요.
examples.en: This lake looks blue-green depending on the weather.

explain: '청록색'만 쓰기도 하고 '청록'이라고만 줄여 말하기도 해요. '민트색'은 더 연하고 밝은 색을 말할 때 쓰는 편이에요. '색을 띠다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You can say '청록색' or shorten it to just '청록'. '민트색' tends to be used for a lighter, brighter shade. It often appears with '색을 띠다' (to take on a color).

examples.ko: 장 본 짐을 차 트렁크에 넣어요.
examples.en: I put the groceries I bought in the car trunk.
The trunk is small, so the bag does not fit.

examples.ko: 짐을 실어야 하니까 트렁크를 열어 주세요.
examples.en: I need to load the luggage, so please open the trunk.

examples.ko: 비가 오는데 우산을 트렁크에 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: It is raining, but I left my umbrella in the trunk.
This car has a spacious trunk.
Dad took the camping chairs out of the trunk.

explain: 한국어에서 트렁크는 보통 승용차 뒤쪽 짐 넣는 곳을 말해요. 여행 가방은 '캐리어'라고 하고, 트럭 뒤쪽은 '짐칸'이라고 해요. 영어의 trunk처럼 코끼리 코나 나무줄기로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In Korean 트렁크 usually means the storage space at the back of a car. A suitcase is a '캐리어', and the back of a truck is a '짐칸'. It is not used for an elephant's trunk or a tree trunk like in English.

examples.en: I went to a seaside guesthouse with my family.
The guesthouse is clean and quiet.
I booked a guesthouse with my friends.

examples.ko: 이 펜션은 마당에서 바비큐를 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this guesthouse you can have a barbecue in the yard.
I stayed one night at a guesthouse and came back.
You have to book a guesthouse just like a hotel.

explain: 한국에서 '펜션'은 보통 산이나 바다 근처에 있는 작은 숙소예요. 영어 'pension'은 보통 연금을 가리키니까 한국어 쓰임과 달라요. 한 채를 빌려 가족이나 친구끼리 묵는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea '펜션' is usually a small lodging near mountains or the sea. The English word 'pension' normally means a retirement pension, so the Korean usage is different. Families or friends often rent a whole house.

examples.en: That athlete has great running form.
Form matters most when you work out.
My friend struck a pose for the photo.

examples.ko: 골프 폼에 문제가 있어서 고치고 있어요.
examples.en: My golf form has a problem, so I'm fixing it.
Today I went out dressed stylishly.
My condition is good lately, so my form has improved.

explain: 영어 form에서 온 말로, 운동 자세를 말할 때와 겉모습이 멋있을 때 써요. 서류의 '양식'을 뜻하는 form은 '폼'보다 '양식'이나 '서식'이라고 하는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 멋있어 보이려고 일부러 자세나 표정을 꾸밀 때 써요. 조금 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone deliberately arranges their posture or expression to look cool. It can sound a little teasing.

explain_en: It comes from English 'form' and is used for exercise posture and for looking cool. For a document form, 양식 or 서식 is more natural than 폼.

examples.ko: 서울에서 부산으로 가는 다음 항공편은 몇 시예요?
examples.en: What time is the next flight from Seoul to Busan?
The flight was canceled, so I stayed one more day.
There are many flights to Jeju Island.
This flight I booked is a direct flight.
In the vacation season, please book your flight in advance.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 항공편이 두 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the flight was delayed by two hours.

explain: '비행기'는 타는 물건 자체이고, 항공편은 정해진 시간표의 한 편을 말해요. '항공편이 취소됐어요', '항공편을 예약했어요'처럼 쓰고, 표 자체는 '항공권'이라고 해요. 소포를 '항공편으로 보내다'처럼 비행기로 보낸다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: '비행기' is the plane itself, while 항공편 is one scheduled flight on a timetable. You say '항공편이 취소됐어요' (the flight was canceled) or '항공편을 예약했어요' (I booked a flight), and the ticket itself is '항공권'. It can also mean 'by air', as in a parcel sent '항공편으로'.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 새 제품을 위해 협력해요.
examples.en: The two companies cooperate on a new product.
Everyone worked together and finished early.
I want to cooperate with my neighbors.
It is nice to see them cooperating.
I hope we can keep cooperating in the future.
If we do not cooperate, the work gets delayed.

explain: '같이하다'가 단순히 함께하는 것이라면, '협력하다'는 같은 목표를 위해 서로 힘을 보태는 느낌이에요. 회사, 나라, 팀 사이에서 많이 써요. 명사 '협력'은 '협력을 부탁하다'처럼 쓰고요.
explain_en: While '같이하다' just means doing something together, '협력하다' means pooling effort for a shared goal. It is common between companies, countries and teams. The noun '협력' appears in phrases like '협력을 부탁하다'.
